title: Rhizoctonia Damping Off Disease of Crucifer Vegetables

Header: Rhizoctonia Damping Off Disease of Crucifer Vegetables
Rhizoctonia solani , Pythium spp. , Fusarium spp. , Alternaria spp. , Phytophthora spp. also cause damping off disease.

Prevention: Avoid fields with a history of the disease.
Avoid excessive watering and nitrate fertilisation.
Plant on raised beds which provide good drainage to prevent waterlogged conditions and reduce moisture saturation in the root zone.
As free water is important for distribution and development of the diseases, efforts to reduce soil moisture will help to reduce disease severity.
Solarisation of soil – cover with polythene sheeting to heat by sunlight for up to a week.
Monitoring: Monitor fields regularly – at weekly intervals.
Look for die back of seedlings.
Spray fungicides when you detect infestation to protect seedlings from fresh attack.
Direct Control: Remove the disease seedlings and destroy, as there is no cure for plants that already have damping off.
Restrictions: Spray fungicide as soon as disease infestation is observed
IV (U) (Unlikely to present acute health hazard)
